core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case (proof lines 11815-11817): by the locality of constructibility the assertion may be checked after base change, so the author assumes X and Y affine.

Reduce to a partition (proof lines 11818-11821): by the characterization recalled above it suffices to produce a finite partition of X by constructible locally closed subschemes on which the pulled back sheaf is finite locally constant.
Produce the partition (proof lines 11822-11824): the author takes the pullback of a partition of Y adapted to F and uses that pullback preserves locally constant sheaves.
proof_roadmap: Use locality of constructibility to assume X and Y affine.
Recall that constructibility is equivalent to being finite locally constant on a finite constructible partition.
Pull back a partition of Y adapted to the given sheaf and invoke the compatibility of pullback with locally constant sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the pullback of a constructible sheaf of sets, of abelian groups or of Lambda-modules under an arbitrary morphism of schemes is again constructible, Lambda being Noetherian (statement lines 11807-11813). The proof is a complete reduction chain: locality of constructibility reduces to X and Y affine (proof lines 11815-11817); the characterization of constructible sheaves on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme by finite constructible partitions reduces the assertion to naming such a partition of X (proof lines 11818-11821); and the author produces it as the pullback of a partition of Y adapted to the given sheaf, invoking the compatibility of pullback with locally constant sheaves (proof lines 11822-11824). The non-formal content is the choice of the partition and the reduction steps. The claim is H2: a structured reduction with every input named.
